ingredients.cook_qty: 130 g for the soup + 20 g to toast

instructions: The night before, or at least 2 hours ahead: remove the crusts and tear the bread into pieces. Put 130 g of the almonds, the bread, garlic, 1/2 cup of the olive oil, sherry vinegar, 2 1/2 cups of cold water, the salt and the pepper in a large bowl.
Cover the bowl and chill it for at least 2 hours, so the bread and almonds soften.
Blend everything until it's completely smooth, working in two batches if your blender is small. This can take a couple of minutes.
Taste it. Add a pinch more salt or a splash more vinegar if it's flat. If it's thicker than you like, stir in a little cold water. Chill it again until you're ready to eat.
Slice the remaining 20 g of almonds. Toast them in a dry skillet over medium heat for about 1 minute, stirring, until they smell nutty. Transfer them to a small bowl.
Stir the soup well and ladle it into bowls. Top each bowl with the grapes, the toasted almonds and a drizzle of the last tbsp of olive oil.
To pack it for lunch, keep the soup in a lidded jar in the fridge for up to 2 days, and add the grapes and almonds when you eat it. Shake or stir it first.
advance_prep_notes: chill at least 2 hours, or the night before
method_notes: No version of this soup shows a rating, so this is a fallback lead: The Spanish Chef's (150 g almonds, 75 g bread, 1 small garlic clove, 125 ml oil, 2 tbsp sherry vinegar, everything chilled together before blending, grapes to finish). Andalucia.com's Malaga version blends a soaked bread paste with 3 cloves of garlic and 1 litre of water for 200 g of almonds; the lead's 400 ml of water would be very thick, so the water is raised to 2 1/2 cups (600 ml) toward that ratio and the garlic to 2 cloves. Both serve it cold with grapes. Gluten-free was not asked for, so ordinary bread is used.
